TASK ID: vertex-cover-to-independent-set

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-m0jiryeg

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

+"""Reduction from Vertex Cover to Independent Set.
+
+The source problem (``VertexCover``) asks whether a given undirected graph
+has a vertex cover of size **at most** ``k``.  The target problem
+(``IndependentSet``) asks whether the same graph has an independent set of
+size **at least** ``k``.
+
+For any graph ``G = (V, E)`` the complement of a vertex cover is an
+independent set and vice‑versa:
+
+    C is a vertex cover  ⇔  V \ C is an independent set.
+
+Therefore a vertex cover of size ``k`` exists iff an independent set of size
+``|V| - k`` exists.  The reduction simply keeps the graph unchanged and
+transforms the parameter ``k`` accordingly.
+
+The function ``reduce`` below implements this transformation.  It runs in
+linear time with respect to the size of the instance (it merely copies the
+edge list) and satisfies all edge‑case requirements inherited from the
+problem specifications.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Dict, List, Any
+
+
+def reduce(instance: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Reduce a Vertex Cover instance to an Independent Set instance.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    instance:
+        A dictionary with keys ``"n"`` (number of vertices), ``"edges"`` (a
+        list of ``[u, v]`` pairs) and ``"k"`` (the size bound for the vertex
+        cover).  The instance is assumed to be validated by the ``VertexCover``
+        class – the reduction does not perform its own validation to keep the
+        implementation lightweight.
+
+    Returns
+    -------
+    dict
+        An Independent Set instance with the same graph and parameter
+        ``k' = n - k``.
+    """
+
+    n: int = instance["n"]
+    k: int = instance["k"]
+    edges: List[List[int]] = instance["edges"]
+
+    # Transform the parameter: a vertex cover of size ≤ k exists ⇔ an
+    # independent set of size ≥ n - k exists.
+    new_k: int = n - k
+
+    # Return a new dict.  ``edges`` is a list of lists; a shallow copy is
+    # sufficient because the inner lists contain only immutable ints.
+    return {
+        "n": n,
+        "edges": [edge.copy() for edge in edges],
+        "k": new_k,
+    }
+
*** End Patch
PATCH"}
